title: Taizong Loses His Mirror
text:
Emperor Taizong, who ruled Tang China from 626 to 649, had come to power by killing two of his brothers. One of the advisers he inherited from his murdered elder brother was Wei Zheng, a minister who had once urged that Taizong be dealt with. Taizong kept him and made him a senior official.

Wei Zheng became famous for criticizing the emperor to his face. Historical records describe him submitting hundreds of remonstrances, against costly building projects, hunting trips, harsh punishments and the emperor's moods. Taizong often grew angry, but he usually accepted the advice.

When Wei Zheng died in 643, Taizong mourned him deeply. According to the Old Book of Tang, he said that with bronze as a mirror one can straighten one's clothes, with history as a mirror one can understand the rise and fall of states, and with people as a mirror one can see one's own successes and mistakes. He had kept all three mirrors, he said, and now one of them was lost.
lesson: Keep near you at least one person who will tell you plainly when you are wrong, and protect them when it stings.
people: Emperor Taizong of Tang, Wei Zheng
source: Old Book of Tang (Jiu Tang Shu), Biography of Wei Zheng; Wu Jing, Zhenguan Zhengyao
